prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1417; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane of a multi-lane roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, and was turning left at an intersection when the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through the same intersection. Upon arrival, I observed that the damage to Driver 1's vehicle was largely consistent with the angle and force of the impact described by both drivers. Driver 2 stated, without hesitation, that the collision occurred just as Driver 1 described it, and two independent witnesses gave statements that matched this account. Scene photographs taken at the time support the same sequence of events. A Passenger was also present in Driver 1's vehicle and was confirmed by both witnesses and responding officers. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee, which I noted is consistent with the way the driver's side door and footwell were deformed during the collision. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to any party at the scene. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
